title: API key is a literal in client-side JavaScript
evidence: api.js:3 defines the key; index.html:25 ships api.js to every visitor; api.js:6 and :11 send it as a Bearer token from the browser. README.md:6 claims 'the API key never leaves the server', which the code contradicts.
failing_case: Anyone opens the page source or DevTools Network tab and reads the Authorization header, then calls /orders and /refunds with the same key and refunds any order.
remediation: Remove the key from the bundle, rotate it, and proxy calls through a server that holds the key and enforces who may refund. Correct README.md:6 until that is true.

title: refund() reports success without waiting for or checking the request
evidence: api.js:11 calls fetch without await and discards the promise; api.js:12 returns ok:true at once. app.js:51 then shows 'Refunded N orders!'. Driven with the refunds endpoint answering 500: POST sent, toast still read 'Refunded 2 orders!'.
failing_case: Select two orders, click Refund selected while the API returns 500 or the network is down. The toast says 'Refunded 2 orders!' and nothing was refunded. A network error also becomes an unhandled rejection.
remediation: await the fetch, check res.ok, return the server's result or throw, and show the failure with a cause and a retry in app.js.

title: Customer name from the API is written into innerHTML unescaped
evidence: app.js:32 interpolates o.customer.name and o.id (data-id) into a template assigned to innerHTML. Driven: a customer named on a visible row ran the handler (window.__xss === 1).
failing_case: A customer registers with the name . When any staff member views the page, the script runs with the page's origin and can read the Bearer token from api.js and call /refunds.
remediation: Build rows with createElement and textContent, or escape every interpolated value at this sink; also set dataset.id through the DOM API.

title: Selection list only grows: unchecked, duplicated and off-screen orders are refunded
evidence: app.js:35 pushes on check and never removes on uncheck; renderTable (app.js:30-36) rebuilds unchecked boxes while selected stays; selected is never cleared after refund (app.js:49-52). Driven: check row 1, uncheck it, check row 2, click Refund: POST body was {"ids":["11","12"]}.
failing_case: Tick order 11 by mistake, untick it, tick order 12, click Refund. Order 11 is refunded too. Ticking the same box twice sends the id twice. Changing page or search shows empty boxes while earlier ids are still queued.
remediation: Keep selection as a Set keyed by id, update it on both check and uncheck, render checkbox state from it, and clear it on filter change and after a confirmed refund.

title: The main action is a span: not focusable, no button role
evidence: index.html:19 uses a span with a click handler set in app.js:49. Driven: focus() on #refundBtn left document.activeElement on BODY; it cannot be reached with Tab or triggered with Enter/Space. WCAG 2.1.1 and 4.1.2 (level A).
failing_case: A keyboard or screen-reader user cannot refund anything, and the control is not announced as a button.
remediation: Use <button type="button" id="refundBtn">, keep the .refund styling and add a disabled state.

quote: - **Fully accessible:** meets WCAG 2.1 AA, including 44 px touch targets (criterion 2.5.5).
title: Accessibility claim is false, and 2.5.5 is a AAA criterion, not part of AA
evidence: Measured: Prev/Next are 32.7 x 18 px (styles.css:18 font-size 12px, padding 2px 4px); the checkboxes use the default size. 2.5.5 Target Size is Level AAA in WCAG 2.1, so it does not make a page 'AA'. The page fails 2.1.1, 1.3.1, 1.4.1, 1.4.3, 2.4.7, 4.1.3 (see the findings above).
failing_case: A buyer or procurement reviewer relies on 'meets WCAG 2.1 AA' and accepts the product; users with keyboards or screen readers cannot refund an order.
remediation: Remove the claim until an audit passes. If the target-size goal stays, state the level correctly (2.5.5 AAA; 2.5.8 24 px is AA in WCAG 2.2) and enlarge the buttons to 44 px.

quote: 12 seats on annual billing at 20% off is $1,440 a year.
title: Pricing arithmetic is wrong: $15 x 12 seats x 12 months at 20% off is $1,728
evidence: Computed: 15 x 12 = 180 a month; x 12 = 2,160 a year; x 0.8 = 1,728. $1,440 equals 2,160 x 2/3 (a 33% discount) or 8 months of 180. If $15 is per seat per year, the figure would be $144. Either way $1,440 is not 20% off.
failing_case: A customer is quoted $1,440, or finance books it, and the invoice later says $1,728 (a $288 dispute per 12-seat account).
remediation: State the billing period of the $15 and print the recomputed figure ($1,728 a year if monthly), or state the discount that gives $1,440.

quote: - Refunds are confirmed before they are sent.
title: README says refunds are confirmed first; the click handler sends the refund at once
evidence: app.js:49-51: onclick calls refund(selected) directly. No confirm(), no dialog, no summary of what will be refunded. Driven: one click produced the POST. 'Confirmed' may also mean the server confirms; the toast is not shown from a server result either (api.js:12).
failing_case: Operator mis-clicks the Refund selected control with 2 rows selected: the refund request is sent with no prompt and no undo.
remediation: Add a confirmation step naming the count and total, or change the README. Keep refunds undoable until the server confirms.

title: Divide by zero: an empty result shows $NaN as AVG ORDER
evidence: Driven: after a search that returned [] the stats row read '$0.00 REVENUE 0 ORDERS $NaN AVG ORDER'. No empty-state text appears in the table either.
failing_case: The user types a customer name with no match, or an account has no orders on first run. The dashboard shows $NaN.
remediation: Return 0 when orders.length is 0 and show an 'No orders match' row with a Clear filters action.

title: Pagination off by one: page starts at 1 but slices from index 10
evidence: app.js:3 sets page = 1; app.js:27 multiplies by PAGE_SIZE with no -1. Driven with 25 orders: 'Page 1 of 2' shows orders 11-20 first; orders 1-10 are never reachable.
failing_case: Load 25 orders. The first ten (usually the newest) are never displayed, and the 5 on the last page are shown as page 2 of '2' only after Next, so they appear on 'Page 2' but 'Page 3' is empty.
remediation: Use (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE, or make page zero-based and display page + 1.

title: Order status is shown only as a coloured dot
evidence: app.js:32 renders an empty span; styles.css:17 gives it green, red or yellow. No text or title. WCAG 1.4.1 (A), 1.1.1. The red/green pair is also indistinguishable for common colour blindness.
failing_case: A colour-blind or screen-reader user cannot tell a paid order from a refunded one in the table.
remediation: Print the status word next to the dot, or give the dot role=img and an aria-label.

title: A failed or non-JSON orders response breaks the page with no message
evidence: api.js:6-7 never checks res.ok and returns res.json(). app.js:41 has no try/catch. Driven with a 500 reply: console 'orders is not iterable', stats empty, the old table stays, user sees nothing.
failing_case: The API is down or the key is rejected (401). The dashboard shows stale or blank data with no error and an unhandled promise rejection.
remediation: Check res.ok in getOrders and throw; catch in load(), keep consistent state and show an error message with a Retry control.

title: Every keystroke fires a request and responses are applied in arrival order
evidence: app.js:45 calls load on each input event with no debounce or abort; app.js:41-42 applies whatever returns last.
failing_case: Type 'al' then 'ali'; the 'al' response is slow and arrives after 'ali'. The table and stats show results for 'al' while the box says 'ali'. A refund then targets rows the user did not search for.
remediation: Debounce input, and use an AbortController or request counter so only the latest response is rendered.

title: Prev and Next have no bounds, so the pager walks to empty and negative pages
evidence: app.js:47-48 change page unconditionally and the buttons are never disabled. Driven: three Next clicks gave 'Page 4 of 2' with an empty table; six Prev clicks gave 'Page -2 of 2' with rows from slice(-20,-10), a wrong set of orders.
failing_case: A user clicks Prev on page 1 or Next on the last page. They see an empty table or the wrong orders under a nonsense page number.
remediation: Clamp page between 1 and the page count and disable Prev/Next at the ends.

title: Refund fires on one click with no confirmation, and the README says it is confirmed
evidence: app.js:49-52 goes straight to refund(selected). No confirm or dialog exists in app.js or index.html. README.md:9 states 'Refunds are confirmed before they are sent'. An empty selection also sends a refund POST with ids: [] and shows 'Refunded 0 orders!'.
failing_case: Click Refund selected once by accident: the POST goes out immediately. Click it with nothing selected: a POST with an empty list is sent and the toast says 'Refunded 0 orders!'.
remediation: Disable the button when nothing is selected and show a confirmation naming the count and total before sending; fix README.md:9 if you ship without it.

title: Search, status filter and row checkboxes have no accessible name
evidence: index.html:17 uses a placeholder as the only label; index.html:18 has no label on the select; app.js:32 renders checkboxes with no label or aria-label; the first th (index.html:21) is empty. WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2.
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'checkbox' with no name, so the user cannot tell which order a checkbox refunds.
remediation: Add a <label> (or aria-label) for #q and #status, and an aria-label such as 'Select order <id> for <name>' on each checkbox.

title: Grey #aaa on white at 11px (2.32:1) and pale lilac on indigo (2.5:1) fail contrast
evidence: Computed: #aaa on #fff = 2.32:1 (.lbl at styles.css:9 and every button at styles.css:18, including Prev/Next at 12px). #c7c2f0 on #6366f1 = 2.64:1 and on #8b5cf6 = 2.50:1 (.eyebrow, styles.css:4, 11px). White on #8b5cf6 (.refund, styles.css:12) is 4.23:1 at the normal text size, under 4.5:1. WCAG 1.4.3 (AA).
failing_case: The REVENUE / ORDERS / AVG ORDER captions, the pager buttons, the eyebrow text and the Refund label are hard to read for low-vision users and in sunlight.
remediation: Use #595959 or darker for the captions and buttons (7:1 on white), a text colour with 4.5:1 or better on the gradient, and a darker purple (#6d28d9) behind white text. Raise text from 11px to at least 12px.

title: Fixed 1000px table and three-column card grid force sideways scroll on a phone
evidence: Driven at 390px wide: document scrollWidth was 1024. styles.css:6 keeps three columns, no media queries exist.
failing_case: On a 390px phone the whole page scrolls horizontally; the Status column and the toolbar sit off screen.
remediation: Use width: 100% with an overflow-x:auto wrapper (or stacked rows), and set .cards to one column below about 600px.

title: Focus outline removed from all buttons, inputs and selects with no replacement
evidence: Driven: while tabbing through the checkboxes getComputedStyle(activeElement).outlineStyle was 'none'. No :focus-visible rule exists anywhere in styles.css. WCAG 2.4.7 (AA).
failing_case: A keyboard user tabbing through the 10 row checkboxes, Prev, Next, search and filter cannot see where focus is.
remediation: Delete the rule, or replace it with :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1a1a1a; outline-offset: 2px } with at least 3:1 against the background.

title: Refund can be submitted twice and the list is not refreshed afterwards
evidence: The handler (app.js:49-52) neither disables the button nor clears selected, and does not call load() after success, so the table and stats still show the old statuses.
failing_case: Double-click Refund selected, or click again after the toast: the same ids are POSTed again, refunding orders twice if the API is not idempotent. The stats still show the orders as paid.
remediation: Disable the button while in flight, send an idempotency key, clear the selection on success and reload orders.

title: Search text is put into the URL without encoding
evidence: api.js:6 interpolates the raw input. Driven: typing 'a&status=refunded#x' requested '/orders?q=a&status=refunded' - the typed text added its own status parameter and the # dropped the real status filter.
failing_case: A user searches for 'Smith & Sons' or 'R#5': the query is cut at & or #, so results are wrong. A crafted string overrides the status filter.
remediation: Build the query with URLSearchParams or encodeURIComponent for both values.

title: Pricing, tax and discount rules live in the render function, and revenue covers only the filtered set
evidence: app.js:9-17 hold the 8.25% tax, 10% gold discount and sign rules inside renderStats, using float multiplication and toFixed for money. The table at app.js:32 shows the raw o.total, so the two screens disagree. orders is the filtered search result, so 'REVENUE' changes with the search box.
failing_case: A gold customer's $100 order shows $100 in the table but counts as $97.43 in revenue. Searching one customer makes 'REVENUE' show that customer's total.
remediation: Move the money rules to one pure, tested function (integer cents), and compute headline revenue from unfiltered data or label it as filtered.

title: Page count rounds down, and Prev/Next and new searches are not bounded
evidence: app.js:34 uses floor, app.js:47-48 decrement and increment with no limits, and load() never resets page. Driven: Prev twice shows 'Page -1 of 2'; Next five times shows 'Page 4 of 2' with 0 rows; 0 orders shows 'Page 1 of 0'.
failing_case: With 25 orders the label reads 'of 2' though there are 3 pages. Go to page 2, search for something with 3 results: the table is empty because page is still 2.
remediation: Use Math.max(1, Math.ceil(n / PAGE_SIZE)), clamp page in the handlers, disable Prev/Next at the ends, and reset page to 1 in load().

title: Page count uses floor, so the last partial page is omitted from 'Page X of Y'
evidence: Driven: 25 orders gave 'Page 1 of 2' with 3 pages of data; 10,000 orders gave 'Page 1 of 1000' (correct only for exact multiples). Fewer than 10 orders gives 'of 0'.
failing_case: 25 orders: the label says 2 pages, the third page of 5 orders exists. 9 orders: 'Page 1 of 0'.
remediation: Use Math.max(1, Math.ceil(orders.length / PAGE_SIZE)).

title: Refund with nothing selected still posts and toasts 'Refunded 0 orders!'
evidence: Driven: with selected = [] a click on the refund control produced the toast 'Refunded 0 orders!' and a POST with {"ids":[]}. The control has no disabled state (styles.css:12). Also 'order(s)' pluralises wrongly for 1 ('Refunded 1 orders!'), and the exclamation mark states success for something unverified.
failing_case: User clicks Refund selected before choosing anything: success toast for zero refunds, and an empty request is sent.
remediation: Disable the control until at least one order is selected; plural-correct copy; message only after a confirmed 2xx, e.g. 'Refunded 2 orders. Total $120.00'.

title: Toast is not a live region and never goes away
evidence: index.html:23 has no role=status or aria-live; app.js:51 only sets display:block and never hides it. WCAG 4.1.3 (AA).
failing_case: A screen-reader user clicks refund (if they could reach it) and hears nothing. A sighted user sees the toast stay on screen for every later action, including after a different refund.
remediation: Add role="status" aria-live="polite", hide it after a timeout or on dismiss, and use a separate error variant.

title: Toast pulses forever with no reduced-motion option
evidence: styles.css:20-21 scale 1 to 1.05 on an infinite loop; no prefers-reduced-motion media query exists. WCAG 2.2.2 (A) for motion over five seconds with no pause; 2.3.3 (AAA).
failing_case: A user with vestibular sensitivity sees a permanently pulsing box in the corner after the first refund.
remediation: Drop the infinite animation; if kept, run it once and disable it under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).
